header.title: How to Test a Refrigerator Start Relay
header.description: This guide provides step-by-step instructions on how to diagnose a faulty refrigerator start relay. Learn how to safely disconnect power, locate the relay, access it, and use a multimeter to test its functionality.

steps.description: Disconnect the refrigerator from the electrical source to prevent electrical shock and ensure accurate testing.
actions: Turn off the circuit breaker
Unplug the unit

steps.description: Locate the start relay by finding the compressor and identifying the box with wires connected to it.
actions: Locate the start relay.
Find the compressor.
Remove the refrigerator from the wall.
Protect the kitchen flooring with cardboard if necessary.
Look for a large cylinder-shaped object with copper tubings connected to it (the compressor).
Move to the right side of the compressor.
Look for a box with wires jutting out of it.
Identify the start relay inside the box.

steps.description: Remove the start relay from inside the control box by first accessing the box and then carefully pulling out the relay.
actions: Loosen the box cover with a screwdriver, if necessary.
Manually loosen tension clips or retaining clips to remove the box cover.
Locate the start relay inside the box.
Pull off the wire-wound relay with needle-nose pliers.

steps.description: This step describes how to test the functionality of a relay using a multimeter by checking continuity between its terminals.
actions: Find the "s" and "m" plug-type terminals and the "L" slip-on terminal.
Position the relay on the floor, counter or table so the "s" and "m" terminal are facing down.
Insert the multi-tester with one probe on each of the "s" and "m" terminals.
Set the tester to zero ohms.
Turn over the relay.
Observe for a clicking sound.
Check the reading should change to "infinity".
Turn the unit over again.
Place one probe from the "s" terminal to the "L" terminal.
Check the tester should read "zero" again.
Observe for no change in the reading.
